The break-even column (Sweep 4) is not right as stated: the pair-minus-inline difference is a sawtooth (each battery swap adds 3 min of labour and scout time), so it crosses zero several times, and E.bisect over [0.005, 200] returns whichever root bisection lands on. evidence.craft: Read econ.py (82 lines), run.py (101), test_econ.py, test_pair.py, figure.py and diffed model.py. econ.py is small and clear with ASSUMED constants named. Defects: model.py is a third-generation verbatim copy (fieldtour -> scoutpair -> pairprice) rather than an import, so a fix upstream does not reach here; run.py model() routes keyword arguments by hand-filtered whitelists and pops an unused 'held_too' key, and calls model() twice per bisection step inside a lambda; bisect() silently returns one root of a function it never checks is monotone; no seed spread or interval is carried from 20 seeds into any cost ratio. 2.
evidence.claims: Backed: 'every price is an assumed round number' (econ.py ASSUMED block, README limitations); R2 >= 0.9999; every Sweep 3 and Sweep 5 ratio quoted; 'model.py copied unchanged' (docstring only); 'simulation only'. Not backed or wrong: 'The break-even field size is 0.54 ha at 2,500, 0.81 at 4,000 and 1.28 at 6,000' presents single values where the difference crosses zero 3 to 7 times (roots.py); 'it breaks even only for a scout at 1,500 USD or less (2.65 ha)' is extrapolated beyond the 1.62 ha simulated range and not marked so, and has nine crossings from 2.08 ha; the Sweep 5 explanation 'few hours make capital dominate, where the pair's cheaper machines win' names the wrong mechanism: the pair's capital is 6,000 against 5,000, and it wins on capital per hectare (4.83 against 11.38 USD/ha, recompute.py) because each machine is occupied fewer minutes per hectare; README says about 15 min to run; the full re-run took 2 min 29 s (stale). 2.
evidence.fitness: A researcher building on this gets a clean cost function and a reproducible sim, but the result does not stand as a finding: (1) the scout's 56.8 flight min/ha are not charged as a person's time (econ.py:15 'supervision is not charged'), yet a remote pilot must watch a drone flight under FAA Part 107 (14 CFR 107.31, visual line of sight); charging it at the same 20 USD/h makes the pair 2.46x the inline robot at 0.72 ha and 2.32x at 20 ha, with no break-even at any size (recompute.py) - the headline flips; (2) both architectures kill about 34% of weeds per pass (Sweep 1), far below any efficacy a grower pays for, so 'cost per hectare' is for a job nobody would buy, and the repeated-pass or slower-speed cost at 90% control is not modelled; (3) the inline and treater ground robots run 150-370 min per field with no charging or battery labour while the scout's swaps are charged, an asymmetry favouring the inline robot; (4) no prior work on robot or drone-guided weeding economics is cited (Pedersen et al. 2006 Precision Agriculture 7:295; Lowenberg-DeBoer et al. 2020 Precision Agriculture 21:278; Shockley et al. 2019 on autonomous-machine economics; ASABE D497 for cost coefficients), so novelty is unstated; (5) it is not part of any programme in research/PROGRAMMES.md. 1.
evidence.domain: Against ASABE EP496/D497 machinery costing: the 30%/yr capital charge is in range (CRF at 8% over 5 years is 0.25, 0.22 with 20% salvage; recompute.py), and charging capital per occupied hour is the standard convention, so the costing skeleton is sound. Departures a farm-machinery economist would hit first: operator/pilot time per machine-hour omitted for the drone (it decides the result); prices are invented round numbers although public ones exist (commercial weeding robots and mapping drones list publicly and differ from 5,000/2,500/3,500 by up to an order of magnitude), against research/CLAUDE.md 'take each parameter that drives a headline result from a datasheet ... When nothing exists, sweep the plausible range' - Sweep 5 sweeps one factor at a time, not jointly; efficacy not held at an agronomic target; single 'break-even' reported for a non-monotone cost difference. 1.

verdict: The cost arithmetic is right: an independent numpy refit of Sweep 1 and my own cost formula reproduce every Sweep 3 and Sweep 5 number, and the experiment re-runs. The finding is not sound. Its one decisive omission is the drone pilot's time: charging the scout's 56.8 flight min/ha at the subject's own 20 USD/h turns 'pair cheaper above 0.54 ha' into 'pair 2.3 to 2.5 times dearer at every size'. The reported break-even sizes are arbitrary roots of a sawtooth cost difference (up to nine crossings), the comparison is at 34% weed kill, prices are invented where public ones exist, and no robot-economics prior work is cited. Tests cover econ.py's helpers but not run.py; 2 of 4 seeded mutants survive. Does not meet the bar (correctness 2, claims 2, verification 2, median 2).
